minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 16, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:03
p.m., on March 16, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 11, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with the City's Real Property Negotiators and Attorney (City Manager
  Dennis Wilberg and City Attorney William P. Curley) Pursuant to Government

City Council Minutes  1  March 16, 2009
   Code Section 54956.8 Concerning the Real Property Known as Turf Lane Park
  Located at 25361 Turf Avenue (APN 619-331-35) in the City of Mission Viejo. The
  Negotiating Parties Are the City of Mission Viejo and the Timberline Community
  Association. Under Negotiation Will Be the Price and Terms of Payment for the
  Potential Sale of the Park to the Timberline Community Association.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened in open session at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he gave the City Council a brief update on the status of
the Turf Lane Park matter but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Community of Character Awards

  Mayor Ury and Council Member Kelly presented the Community of Character Awards to
  Anna Boyce and Kathryn Monaghan.

P2.  Recognize Citywide Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Volunteer Service

  Mayor Ury presented certificates of appreciation to Joan Collings for volunteer hours
  with the Senior Community Activity Team (SCAT) and Evelyn Vocila for volunteer
  hours at the Mission Viejo Library. Library volunteers Julie Damon, Pauline Dougherty,
  and Frank Simon were unable to attend the meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry  Gilbert,  M.V.:  encouraged  the  City  Council  Members  to  visit
www.missionviejobusiness.com, a web site developed by members of the Committee for
Integrity in Government to promote business in Mission Viejo. Mr. Gilbert expressed opposition
to the City paying a fee for similar work.

Suzi Scallon, Board Member of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library: announced two
upcoming "Readers Presents" events featuring authors Charles Norm Stevens on March 26,
2009, and Franz Wizner on April 6, 2009. She also reminded residents that Waste Management
will donate, to the Friends of the Library, $5 per ton for all recyclable trash collected during the
month of April and she encouraged residents to recycle as much as possible next month.

City Council Minutes  2  March 16, 2009
 Carolyn Wertheim, Trabuco Canyon: thanked the City Council for honoring Kathryn Monaghan
with a Character Award this evening.

CLOSURE OF O’NEILL ELEMENTARY SCHOOL

Mayor Ury stated that the information the City received on the closure of O’Neill Elementary
School arrived after the posting of the Agenda for tonight’s meeting and there is a need for
immediate action. If the Council wishes to review issues related to the pending closure of
O’Neill Elementary School and/or provide direction to staff, the City Council can entertain a
motion to add this item to the agenda and it must pass with a four-fifths vote.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to declare a
need subsequent to the posting of the agenda to review issues related to the pending closure of
O’Neill Elementary School and to allow the City Council to direct staff to prepare information as
requested by the Council.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

The following discussed the planned closure of O’Neill Elementary School and asked the City
Council to assist in identifying funding solutions to prevent the closing of the school: Linda
DeFonce, M.V.; Denise Morissete, M.V.; Robert Bennett, M.V.; Joan Snow, M.V.; and Romney
Miller, M.V.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to send a
letter to the Saddleback Unified School District Board of Trustees and Administration
Department with copies sent to the Teachers Union and all the teachers in the Saddleback
Unified School District, recommending the idea of a 4% salary reduction for a one year period as
a solution to keeping O’Neill Elementary School open. The letter shall include notation that the
City recently instituted a 1.5% salary reduction for its own employees and a reminder of the
funding that the City provides the District through School Resource Officers, Crossing Guards,
etc. The letter shall also invite the School District to sit down with the City to discuss ideas and
solutions that can achieve the community’s goal of keeping O’Neill School open.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  3  March 16, 2009
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 10, 11, and 12 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the Council’s Housing Workshop of February 24, 2009, as
  presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of March
  2, 2009, as presented.

3.  Summary of Fiscal Year 2008 - 2009 Budget Amendments to Date

  Received and filed.

4.  Check Register dated February 20, 2009, in the amount of $1,674,691.27

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated February 27, 2009, in the amount of $2,582,721.94

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer's Monthly Report for January 2009

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  4  March 16, 2009
 7.  Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for January 2009

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2009

  Received and filed.

9.  Mileage reimbursement requests from former council member Gail Reavis

  Authorized payment of the mileage reimbursement requests received from Gail Reavis
  for the periods October 10, 2008 to October 23, 2008 in the amount of $49.57, October
  24, 2008 to November 6, 2008 in the amount of $19.22, and November 7, 2008 to
  November 20, 2008 in the amount of $13.28.

13.  Air Quality Improvement Special Revenue Fund Financial Statements with Report
  on Audit by Independent Certified Public Accountants for the Fiscal Year Ended
  June 30, 2008 and AB 2766 Annual Program Report, June 30, 2008

  Received and filed.

14.  Single Audit of Federally Assisted Grant Programs for the Fiscal Year Ended June
  30, 2008

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

10.  Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Second Quarter of FY 2008-09

  Council Member Schlicht asked questions of staff regarding account numbers listed in
  the report.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to receive and
  file.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

City Council Minutes  5  March 16, 2009
 11.  Olympiad Road Resurfacing (CIP 202)

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the portion of Olympiad Road that will not be
  slurried at this time.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon stated that the portion of Olympiad from
  Jeronimo to Alicia currently warrants a slurry seal. The City is attempting to obtain
  Federal Stimulus Funds for asphalt overlay from Alicia Parkway to Marguerite Parkway.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  approve the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the
  subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

12.  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the Alicia Parkway Traffic Light
  Synchronization Program Project

  Council Member Schlicht asked if the MOU was a legally binding contract. City
  Attorney Bill Curley responded that it is a binding document.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve
  Memorandum of Understanding C-8-1403 with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority for the Alicia Parkway Traffic Light Synchronization Project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

City Council Minutes  6  March 16, 2009
 16.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Mayor Pro Tem MacLean.

17.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Received the report from Council Member Ledesma.

18.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Received the report from Council Member Kelley.

19.  Discussion Regarding Mission Viejo and its Compliance with Housing Laws

  Mayor Ury asked when the Council can expect to see a report on the concept of First
  Responder Housing. City Attorney Bill Curley stated that Special Counsel Celeste Brady
  is conducting a thorough analysis and the report will come before the Council at the next
  meeting, if not sooner.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is still waiting for density bonus data and
  information on the idea of funding assistance for down payments. City Manager
  Wilberg noted that the information has been distributed and he will see that it is
  transmitted again.

20.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Council Member Schlicht stated that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Roundabout Intersections Committee as the meeting’s agenda was not posted. The next
  meeting will be held on Wednesday, March 18, 2009, at 8:00 a.m.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:10 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:21
p.m. with four City Council Members present; Mayor Pro Tem MacLean returned at 8:23 p.m.

21.  Retail Market Customer Analytic Services in Support of the City and Community
  Development Agency’s Targeted Business Attraction Strategy

  The following presented a written comment in opposition to the proposed contract: Joe
  Holtzman, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  March 16, 2009
   By consensus, the City Council directed that this proposal be returned to the Economic
  Development Ad Hoc Committee for further study and to formulate a recommendation
  for future consideration by the City Council.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

22.  Responses to Questions on the Feb 6, 2009 and Feb 13, 2009 Check Registers

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein outlined the
  questions posed at the prior City Council Meeting and provided answers for the checks in
  question.

City Manager Wilberg announced that he will be absent from the next City Council
Meeting.

City Attorney’s Report

23.  Certification of Petition for the Vote on Private and Public Property Land Use
  Regulation Initiative

  Dale Tyler, M.V.: thanked the thousands of residents who signed the "Vote on Public and
  Private Property Land Use Regulation Initiative" petition and asked the Council to adopt
  the Ordinance and save the City the cost of an election.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  (1) receive the City Clerk’s Certification of Sufficiency for the Vote on Private and
  Public Property Land Use Regulation Initiative petition; (2) direct the City Attorney to
  prepare a report as authorized in California Elections Code Subsection 9215(c) pursuant
  to California Elections Code Section 9212 and return at the City Council Meeting of
  April 6 , 2009; and (3) adopt Resolution 09-08 Amending the Fiscal Year 2008-2009
  Budget in the Amount of $37,485 from Unapproprited Reserves to Pay For the Signature
  Verification Fees for the Vote on Private and Public Property Land Use Regulation
  Initiative.

City Council Minutes  8  March 16, 2009
   Motion was made by Council Member Schlicht to adopt the Ordinance without alteration
  at this meeting or within 10 days. The motion died for lack of a second.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  City Attorney Bill Curley encouraged the Council Members to contact him as soon as
  possible if they wish to see a particular element addressed in the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked the volunteers and Community of Character award winners
who were recognized earlier this evening. She outlined her experience serving as Principal for a
Day at Newhart Middle School and at Mission Viejo High School. She was tremendously
impressed by both schools and very pleased with the improvements that have been made at
Newhart since the City asked for the audit and for funding to come back to that campus. Council
Member Kelley thanked the Principals of the schools for doing a wonderful job and she stated
that both schools are a source of pride here in Mission Viejo.

Council Member Ledesma

Asked the City Attorney to come back with an update on the Saddleback Unified School District
bus route issue.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht referred to a citizen report of continued dumping at lower Curtis Park
and stated that there shouldn’t be any more debris coming from the Crown Valley Parkway
widening project. She referred to a note that indicates the California Fish and Game is seeking
information on this project and asked if the City is violating any environmental laws. Council

City Council Minutes  9  March 16, 2009
 Member Schlicht also asked if there will be further dumping in the City as a result of the Santa
Margarita Water District reservoir project. She requested the City Clerk post the December 15,
2008, Workshop Minutes on the web site and asked when the Election History will be updated.
Council Member Schlicht thanked residents for their continued support and expressed concern
with the Mayor’s procedures for conducting these meetings.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury announced that he had a chance to serve as Principal for a Day at Castille Elementary
School. Principal Lyon did a wonderful job and he was especially impressed with the school’s
specialty autism section. Mayor Ury wished residents of the community a Happy St. Patrick’s
Day.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:43 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, April 6, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 6, 2009

City Council Minutes  10  March 16, 2009
